judged_by: Matched by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent on 2026-11-25; not yet checked by the labeler.

question.note: Spillover onto perceptions (Q1) and onto Democrats' sense of representation (Q3).

central_claim.note: Ad harm and counter-narrative offset; omits the improvement in representation. First quote NOT IN PAPER, second faithful.

evidence.note: Survey experiment via Prolific with 2,439 self-identified Democrats in three named arms (counts not given; calibration judge credited E2 for 'roughly even' arms). E1 without the dates or pre-registration, as in the calibration note.
Least squares with heteroskedasticity-consistent SEs (E5, as in the calibration note). Outcome indices without the ad-support index (partial E4).

key_findings.note: F5: counter-narrative lowered perceived quality of Democratic representation relative to the ad alone. F3 partial: the ad raised quality of representation, but the public-service-motives increase is not stated.
'More damaging for this group' is the paper's own wording (p.14). The main effect of system-impacted status is accurate extra detail.

scope_and_limits.note: Fielded after the election, open for active campaigns (L6). Durability and voting behavior without repeated exposure (partial L5).

theoretical_positioning.note: 'Positions itself within' social categorization theory; no stance word, so no T4.

interlocutor_claim.note: Also gives the [6] finding that Democrats respond more to positive ads; accurate.
